title: Johnny Dodds's temper, jokes and fight habits
summary: Dodds describes his brother's joking, patience, quick temper, and how he acted at prize fights, and his loyalty in staying with him.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Was there ever a time when he was young that he, I know he was always strictly business in the late days, was he ever sort of wild when he was young? No, he never was. Never was. Always was a man to stick to business. Everything he said was low. Was he always a quiet fellow like when I knew him? Well no, he was a joker. He's a big joker too. Yeah. Oh God, he had, he had senses he were. He'd have a joker and he cared, but he's one guy would take it as far as it would go. Take it to the extreme if necessary. And as long as he knew he had a joke, but he'd keep that joke going a long time. And he's a fellow that didn't get disgusted with himself as a joke. But, uh, I have to get so sick of that. And my patients, she's run out very fast. Very fast. But he, he was one of those kinds, he was a long, patient guy. And, uh, which I wasn't. And that made a difference to people. Because he had one way of thinking, I had another way of thinking. But, to pass it all off, I never did get nowhere with mine. I didn't even have to give over to him. It was just, it wasn't nothing. And that was his way. I found a whole lot was wrong with it, but I couldn't dare bring it to other people, because they wouldn't understand. Yeah. Like when you first met us. You thought we were too lovely as a person as a boy. We'd done some recording. Well, I still do. Yeah, but we didn't get lost again. And it wasn't that I did anything, or he did something to me. But we just couldn't see eye to eye. Yeah, I know. A little different type, but I mean, you still got along. Oh, yeah. Like you said, you wouldn't even leave him to go with Joe Oliver. Well, indeed. I mean, you were faithful to him. I wouldn't leave him to go with nobody. I could have got a minute job by myself. And I was the kind that could work with anybody. Of course, he wouldn't believe it. He would believe I was a selfish fellow in the world. But that's what he felt like. Nothing nobody could tell him. It was that, it's that. Did he ever get excited? Did he have a quick temper or anything? Yeah, he had a quick temper. He had a very quick temper. Of course, I had two. One of those kind of things. And oftentimes, we used to fight. But it wasn't the kind of fight that you would think. I get very angry, and he gets very angry. We speak our mind to each other, and double up our fists to fight. Somebody thinks, sure, it's going to be a big fight. But no worth no fight. And for my part, a little while, I'm over it. But he keep it in him all night. All day the next day. If you never make up to him, he'll never make up to you. Well, that's what I didn't like. Well, he's my brother. I knew I had to appreciate him. Because he got all the work. I didn't get any. Oh, you say he was a big baseball fan too. Oh, yeah. What about prize fights? Well, he loved that too. I don't think he'd be throwing the fights the same as the man in the ring. And Houston's out of you got hit. He'd be hitting you. Oh, he'd be hitting you. Every time the guy in the ring hit you. That's right. He's actually going to make the man throw a punch. And he's throwing it right at you. You're going to get it. Actually hit you, huh? Oh, yeah. He hit you. Of course, he was excusing himself. Oh, yeah. Sure. He was cute. Didn't mean it. So wrapped up in the fight. All his emotions. If he was looking at the fight, he'd be in the fight. He'd be as tired as the guy was during the fight. Be tired out after. But I never was that way. I was always emotional, but not that way.
